identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Sarangapani is one of the 108 Divya Desams glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham and one of the five Pancharanga Kshetrams, the Ranganatha-linked Vishnu temples along the Kaveri. Its sanctum is built in the form of a chariot drawn by horses and elephants, evoking the tradition that Vishnu descended from Vaikuntha in such a chariot to marry Lakshmi at this site.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Sarangapani Temple in Kumbakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Vishnu, worshipped here as Sarangapani (also called Aravamudhan) with his consort Komalavalli Thayar, a form of Lakshmi. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams — the Vishnu temples glorified in the Naalayira Divya Prabandham — and is counted among the Pancharanga Kshetrams, the five Ranganatha-linked Vishnu temples along the Kaveri.

The temple's earliest epigraphical evidence dates to the late Chola period (10th–12th century CE), with substantial later contributions from the Vijayanagara Empire and the Nayaks of Madurai. Its eleven-tier rajagopuram rises to roughly 173 feet, and its sanctum is built in the unusual form of a chariot drawn by horses and elephants, evoking Vishnu's descent to earth. The temple underwent a Mahasamprokshanam (re-consecration) on 13 July 2015 and is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
narrative.documentedHistory:
Epigraphical evidence for the temple dates from the late Chola period (10th–12th century CE); Wikipedia's account suggests the site may have functioned as a Vaishnava place of worship as early as the 7th–8th century. The temple's own historical account records contributions at different times from the Medieval Cholas, the Vijayanagara Empire and the Nayaks of Madurai, credited with much of the standing structure, including the sanctum and towers.

The temple follows the Pancharatra Agama and is associated with the Vadakalai tradition of Sri Vaishnavism; it is classed as an Ubaya Pradhana Kshetram, where both the presiding deity (moolavar) and the processional festival deity (utsavar) hold equal ritual importance. A Mahasamprokshanam (ceremonial re-consecration following renovation) was performed on 13 July 2015.

The temple is administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of the Government of Tamil Nadu.
narrative.sthalaPuranam: According to the temple's traditional account, the sage Hema Rishi performed penance on the banks of the Potramarai tank seeking Lakshmi as his daughter. Vishnu, pleased with his devotion, is said to have descended in a chariot drawn by horses and elephants from Vaikuntha to marry Lakshmi, who emerged from the tank amid lotus flowers and became known as Komalavalli. The temple's chariot-shaped sanctum is said to commemorate this descent.

editorial.verificationNotes: No dedicated Tamil Nadu HR&CE (hrce.tn.gov.in) subdomain or temple page could be located for this temple during research, despite Wikipedia stating HR&CE administers it. Practical information here relies on the temple's own informational website (sarangapanitemple.org, technically maintained by a third-party vendor per its Contact page) cross-referenced with Wikipedia; it should be treated as needing recheck rather than government-verified.
